newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's SEZ plans IPO on Zurich bourse.
newsitem.headline: Austria's SEZ plans IPO on Zurich bourse.

text.p: Austrian spin-etch machinery maker SEZ said on Wednesday it was planning to set up a Swiss-based holding company and list almost 50 percent of its equity on the Zurich stock exchange before the end of the year.
"The volume will be around 800 million schillings," chief executive Egon Putzi told journalists at the company's headquarters in the southern resort town of Villach.

Details of the issue, the subscription period and the price would be announced shortly before the issue date, he added. The proceeds would be used to finance the group's expansion plans and to repay existing credits. Bank J. Vontobel & Co. Ltd had been chosen as lead manger, he said.
Putzi said he and his co-chief executive Franz Sumnitsch would maintain a controlling stake in the company, which makes machines used for the production of computer chips.

SEZ reported a net profit of 4.9 million Swiss francs last year on sales of 34.7 million francs. The company expects sales to rise to 43.1 million francs and net profit to 6.9 million francs this year.
In 1997, SEZ said it expects sales to rise to 69 million francs, and profit to almost double to 13.4 million. -- Paul Arnold, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 272
